title: Controls linchpin — personal prep notes for SOC2 mapping
content:
Purpose:
- Quick personal brain dump to map high-risk flows to candidate controls and list what evidence we likely already have vs what we need to generate.
- Not a polished deliverable — iteration step before I hand off to compliance lead.

Topline observations (from recent readiness run):
- Identity and session management is the single largest gap for Dedicated/private customers: audit trails exist but are fragmented between control plane (hosted) and private install docs.
- Automated log retention for console/console-api events often missing in private deployments; docs say "customer-managed" but we need an evidence story.
- Change control (deploy approvals) is present in prod infra but not consistently captured for model rollouts (model version changes).

Risk surface (sketch):
- Unauthorized access to customer data: routes = API keys, tokens, private-deploy credentials.
- Unintended data exposure in logs/metrics (embeddings/debug dumps).
- Incomplete rollback/incident response for model regressions causing PII leakage.
- Misconfigured network controls in on-prem packages.

Candidate control mappings (working):
- Risk: Unauthorized access to customer data --> Control: IAM policy enforcement + key rotation procedures.
  - Evidence: key rotation runbook (exists), recent rotation logs (partial), ticket for rotation automation (ENG-1182).
- Risk: Data exposure in logs --> Control: Log scrubbing & retention policy + CI lint on logging statements.
  - Evidence: log-retention policy doc (hosted), sample sanitized logs (have), CI rule in repo GH-PR-5412 (draft).
- Risk: Model rollout causing regressions --> Control: Model rollout canary + rollbacks + eval baseline checks.
  - Evidence: canary config in console (screenshots), eval-suite results (not centralized), deployment approvals (ad-hoc Slack threads).

Open questions (need answers before first draft control matrix):
- For private deployments, do we require customers to demonstrate they applied our recommended log-retention settings, or do we accept attestation? (work with legal)
- Is there a canonical evidence store for eval suites? If not, should we centralize under /evidence/model-evals/ and script uploads?
- Do infra change approval records (e.g., merge approvals) qualify as change-control evidence or do we need a separate approval ticket?

Quick wins to collect evidence this week:
- Pull last 6 months of key rotation events from KMS and export a CSV. Owner: Ava. (ENG-1182 reference)
- Capture screenshots and export a canary rollout config for model-x-1 from staging. Owner: Lena.
- Add a lightweight metadata flag in eval harness to include commit hash + run id -> store in S3 under /evidence/model-evals/. Owner: me (Jorge).

Things to draft in the upcoming control matrix: acceptance criteria + deterministic tests for each control:
- IAM: evidence must show role change audit + key rotation + at least one successful automated rotation run in last 90 days.
- Logging: evidence must include retention policy doc AND a sanitized log sample + CI rule enforcing scrubbing.
- Change control: for model changes, require a recorded canary run with pass/fail metric + documented rollback executed in at least one prior incident.

Minimal test plan (how we'll verify controls):
1) Sample cross-check: pick 3 dedicated customers, request admin access logs + deployment history, verify keys rotated and access limited.
2) Logging test: deploy a synthetic request that would normally surface parseable content, assert scrubbing rules apply in logs.
3) Model rollout test: push a controlled bad prompt to canary and confirm rollback path triggers and is recorded.

Notes to self:
- Keep language in control descriptions conservative: avoid promising "automated" where only manual process exists.
- For evidence links, prefer stable exports (CSV/PDF) over screenshot-only. Screenshots are ok as temporary artifacts but flag them for later replacement.

Potential showstoppers (escalate):
- If private installs cannot provide proof of log retention, we need an attestation workflow + quarterly spot checks.
- If model evals cannot be tied to commit IDs, then we cannot claim reproducible testing for rollouts (this will block SOC2 for model-change-related controls).

Next actions (my immediate checklist):
- [ ] Draft one-page control matrix for security lead (due 2026-03-12).
- [ ] Export KMS rotation events (Ava) by 2026-03-06.
- [ ] Add eval metadata to harness and run a sample upload (me) by 2026-03-08.
- [ ] Sync w/ legal about attestations for private installs (meeting 2026-03-09).

Slack & ticket refs I keep bumping into:
- #trust-ops: thread "private deploy evidence" (has 3 examples), link pinned in Confluence page above.
- ENG-1182: automation for KMS rotation (PR in progress).

Random thoughts / brainstorming (messy):
- Could we provide a small "evidence kit" script for private customers that collects minimal artifacts: /var/log audit, KMS manifest, installed agent version, model manifest. Ship as tgz they upload during audit. That reduces ambiguity.
- Add a lightweight signed attestation file on private installs that the customer can sign with a local key — may satisfy auditors for some items. But legal will care.
- For model rollouts: consider tagging every model release with a "compliance" label if it touched PII-sensitive training data or has a data-handling opt-in.

Notes to remove/rework before handing over: avoid bullet noise, add table of artifacts, and a mapping to TSC/CC control IDs (I need the canonical mapping).

End of scratchpad.

(If I don't get to this today, handoff to Ava with the KMS export and a short note.)
